sections.text:
Every triangle is **half of a rectangle or parallelogram**.

This right triangle has legs 6 cm and 4 cm. It fits inside a 6 by 4 rectangle with area 24 cm², so the triangle's area is **12 cm²**.

For any triangle, use **A = ½ × b × h**.

The height goes straight up from the base at a square corner. A triangle with base 10 m and height 5 m has area ½ × 10 × 5 = **25 m²**.

Some triangles lean so far that the height lands **outside** the triangle. That's okay!

This one has base 4 in and height 6 in, so its area is still ½ × 4 × 6 = **12 in²**.

learn.keyIdea: Triangle area = ½ × base × height, where the height is straight up from the base.

examples.title: Half of a rectangle
examples.prompt: A right triangle has legs 6 cm and 4 cm. What is its area in square centimeters?

steps.do: Picture a 6 cm by 4 cm rectangle around the triangle: 6 × 4 = 24.
steps.why: The two legs of a right triangle are the sides of a rectangle.

steps.do: Cut the rectangle in half along the slanted side: 24 ÷ 2 = 12.
steps.why: The slanted side splits the rectangle into two matching triangles.

examples.check: Two triangles of 12 make 24, the full rectangle. ✅
examples.mistake: Don't forget to divide by 2, or you get the rectangle's area instead.

examples.title: A leaning triangle
examples.prompt: An obtuse triangle has base 7 in and height 6 in (the height falls outside the triangle). What is its area in square inches?

steps.do: Use the base 7 and the height 6, not a slanted side.
steps.why: The height must be straight up and down from the base line.
Base times height gives the area of the matching parallelogram.
A triangle is half of that parallelogram.

examples.mistake: Measuring along a slanted side instead of the straight-up height makes the answer too big.

examples.title: Working backward
examples.prompt: A triangle has area 24 m² and base 8 m. What is its height in meters?

steps.do: Write the formula with what you know: 24 = ½ × 8 × h.
steps.why: Filling in the formula shows exactly which number is missing.
Taking half of the base first makes the equation simpler.
Division undoes multiplication.

examples.mistake: Don't stop at 24 ÷ 8; that forgets the ½ and gives a height that is too small.

guided.prompt: A right triangle has legs 8 ft and 5 ft. What is its area in square feet?

steps.do: Find the area of the 8 by 5 rectangle.
steps.why: The triangle is exactly half of this rectangle.
The slanted side cuts the rectangle into two equal triangles.

guided.prompt: A triangle has base 9 cm and height 7 cm. What is its area in square centimeters? Type it as an improper fraction.

steps.why: This is the area of the matching parallelogram.
A triangle is half of a parallelogram.

guided.prompt: A house shape is a 10 ft by 6 ft rectangle with a triangle roof on top. The roof has base 10 ft and height 4 ft. What is the total area in square feet?

steps.why: Split the shape into pieces you know.
The roof is a triangle.
The whole area is the sum of its parts.

guided.prompt: A triangle has area 35 in² and base 10 in. What is its height in inches?

steps.why: Doubling undoes the ½ in the formula.
Base times height equals the doubled area.

sections.text:
A **parallelogram** can become a rectangle: cut a triangle off one end and slide it to the other.

This one has base 8 m, height 5 m, and slanted side 6 m. Its area is 8 × 5 = **40 m²**.

A **trapezoid** has two parallel sides. Use **A = ½ × (b₁ + b₂) × h**.

With sides 6 in and 10 in and height 4 in: ½ × 16 × 4 = **32 in²**.

Tricky shape? **Compose** (add pieces) or **decompose** (cut and subtract).

This L shape is a 10 by 8 rectangle with a 4 by 3 corner missing: 80 − 12 = **68 square units**.

learn.keyIdea: Break any polygon into rectangles and triangles, then add (or subtract) their areas.

examples.title: Slide a parallelogram
examples.prompt: A parallelogram has base 9 ft, slanted side 5 ft, and height 4 ft. What is its area in square feet?

steps.do: Pick the base 9 and the height 4; ignore the slanted side 5.
steps.why: Area needs the straight-up height, not the slanted side.
Cutting off a triangle and sliding it over makes a 9 by 4 rectangle.

examples.check: The rectangle made by sliding is 9 × 4 = 36. ✅
examples.mistake: Using the slanted side gives 9 × 5 = 45, which is too big.

examples.title: Trapezoid trick
examples.prompt: A trapezoid has parallel sides 5 cm and 9 cm and height 6 cm. What is its area in square centimeters?

steps.why: Two copies of the trapezoid make a parallelogram with this long base.
That is the area of the double-size parallelogram.
We only want one trapezoid, which is half.

examples.mistake: Don't multiply the two parallel sides together; add them first.

examples.title: Hexagon pieces
examples.prompt: A regular hexagon splits into 6 equal triangles, each with base 6 m and height 5.2 m. What is the hexagon's area in square meters?

steps.why: Decomposing turns a hard shape into easy triangles.
All 6 triangles are the same size.

examples.mistake: Don't forget the ½ for each triangle, or the answer doubles.

guided.prompt: A rectangle is 7 cm long and 4 cm wide. What is its area in square centimeters?

steps.do: Which formula finds the area of a rectangle?
steps.why: Choosing the right formula is the first step.
steps.hint: Area counts squares in rows and columns.

steps.why: There are 7 squares in each of 4 rows.
steps.hint: Multiply the length by the width.

guided.prompt: A parallelogram has base 12 in, slanted side 7 in, and height 5 in. What is its area in square inches?

steps.why: The height is the straight-up distance, not the slanted side.
steps.hint: Look for the length that makes a square corner with the base.

steps.why: Sliding a triangle over turns it into a 12 by 5 rectangle.

guided.prompt: A trapezoid has parallel sides 7 m and 11 m and height 6 m. What is its area in square meters?

steps.why: The two bases work together in the formula.
steps.hint: Add the top and the bottom.

steps.why: This is the area of two copies of the trapezoid.
One trapezoid is half of the two copies.

guided.prompt: An L-shaped garden is a 12 ft by 9 ft rectangle with a 5 ft by 4 ft corner cut out. What is its area in square feet?

steps.why: Start with the full rectangle before the corner was cut.
This piece is not part of the garden.
Taking away the cut corner leaves the L shape.

sections.text:
**Volume** counts how many unit cubes fill a box.

This box is 4 cubes long, 3 wide, and 2 tall. One layer has 4 × 3 = 12 cubes, and 2 layers make **24 cubic units**.

Use **V = l × w × h**, even with fractions!

A box 2½ ft by 2 ft by 3 ft holds 2½ × 2 × 3 = **15 ft³**.

Or use **V = B × h**, where B is the area of the base.

A base of 6 in² and a height of 1½ in gives 6 × 1½ = **9 in³**.

learn.keyIdea: Volume = length × width × height = base area × height, and it works for fraction edges too.

examples.title: Counting cubes
examples.prompt: A box holds 1-cm cubes: 4 long, 3 wide, 2 tall. What is its volume in cubic centimeters?

steps.why: The bottom layer is a rectangle of cubes.
Every layer is the same, so multiply by the number of layers.

examples.mistake: Don't add the edges (4 + 3 + 2); volume multiplies them.

examples.title: Fraction edges
examples.prompt: A box is 2½ ft by 1½ ft by 2 ft. What is its volume in cubic feet? Write it as an improper fraction.

steps.do: Write the mixed numbers as fractions: 2½ = 5/2 and 1½ = 3/2.
steps.why: Improper fractions are easier to multiply.
This is the area of the base.
Each foot of height adds another layer of the base.

examples.mistake: Don't multiply only the whole numbers and drop the fractions.

examples.title: Half-inch cubes
examples.prompt: How many ½-inch cubes fill a box that is 1 in by 1 in by 2 in?

steps.do: Find the box's volume: 1 × 1 × 2 = 2 cubic inches.
steps.why: We need the total space to fill.

steps.do: Find one small cube: ½ × ½ × ½ = ⅛ cubic inch.
steps.why: Each tiny cube has edges of ½ inch.
Eight ½-inch cubes fit in each 1-inch cube, and there are 2 of those.

examples.mistake: A ½-inch cube is ⅛ of a cubic inch, not ½, so the count is bigger than you might think.

guided.prompt: A box holds 1-in cubes: 5 long, 2 wide, and 3 tall. What is its volume in cubic inches?

steps.do: How many cubes are in one layer? (5 × 2)
steps.why: The bottom layer is a rectangle of cubes.
Each layer has the same number of cubes.

guided.prompt: A box is 3½ cm by 2 cm by 4 cm. What is its volume in cubic centimeters?

steps.why: This gives the area of the base.
Height tells how many base layers stack up.

guided.prompt: A prism has base area 12 in² and height 2¼ in. What is its volume in cubic inches?

steps.do: Which formula uses the base area?
steps.why: B already means length × width.
Each inch of height adds a layer with area B.

guided.prompt: A fish tank has volume 22½ ft³. It is 3 ft long and 2½ ft wide. How tall is it in feet?

steps.do: Find the base area: 3 × 2½. Type it as an improper fraction.
steps.why: Volume divided by base area gives the height.
V = B × h, so h = V ÷ B.

sections.text:
When two points share an **x-value**, subtract their y-values to find the distance.

From (2, 1) to (2, 7) is 7 − 1 = **6 units**.

Points on **opposite sides of an axis**? Add their distances to the axis.

From (−4, 3) to (5, 3) is 4 + 5 = **9 units**.

Connect points to make a polygon, then measure its sides.

The rectangle (1, 1), (5, 1), (5, 4), (1, 4) is 4 wide and 3 tall, so its area is **12 square units**.

learn.keyIdea: Same x? Subtract the y's. Same y? Subtract the x's. Opposite sides of an axis? Add the distances.

examples.title: Same x, subtract y
examples.prompt: How many units apart are (3, 2) and (3, 8)?

steps.why: Matching x-values mean the points line up vertically.
The distance is how far apart the y-values are.

examples.mistake: Don't subtract the matching x-values; that gives 0.

examples.title: Across the axis
examples.prompt: How many units apart are (−3, 4) and (5, 4)?

steps.do: Both points have y = 4, so they line up across.
steps.why: Matching y-values mean a horizontal segment.

steps.do: Find each distance to the y-axis: 3 and 5.
steps.why: The axis splits the segment into two parts.
Points on opposite sides of an axis are farther apart, so add.

examples.mistake: 5 − 3 = 2 is wrong because −3 is on the other side of 0.

examples.title: Rectangle perimeter
examples.prompt: A rectangle has vertices (2, 1), (8, 1), (8, 5), and (2, 5). What is its perimeter in units?

steps.why: The bottom side runs between x = 2 and x = 8.
The left side runs between y = 1 and y = 5.
A rectangle has two widths and two heights.

examples.mistake: Don't use the coordinates (8 and 5) as side lengths; subtract to get lengths.

guided.prompt: How many units apart are (1, 5) and (8, 5)?

steps.do: Which coordinate is the same for both points?
steps.why: The matching coordinate tells the direction of the segment.
The distance is the gap between the x-values.

guided.prompt: How many units apart are (2, −6) and (2, 3)?

steps.do: How far is (2, −6) from the x-axis?
steps.why: Distance to an axis is never negative.

steps.do: How far is (2, 3) from the x-axis?
steps.why: This is the other part of the segment.
The points are on opposite sides of the x-axis.

guided.prompt: A rectangle has vertices (−2, 1), (4, 1), (4, 5), and (−2, 5). What is its area in square units?

steps.why: Opposite sides of the y-axis means add 2 + 4.
Subtract the y-values.
Rectangle area is length times width.

guided.prompt: A right triangle has vertices (1, 1), (7, 1), and (1, 5). What is its area in square units?

steps.do: Find the bottom leg from (1, 1) to (7, 1).
steps.why: The legs are the base and height.

steps.do: Find the left leg from (1, 1) to (1, 5).
steps.why: This leg is straight up, so it is the height.
A right triangle is half of a rectangle.

sections.text:
A **net** is a 3D shape unfolded flat. **Surface area** is the total area of every face in the net.

A cube with edge 2 cm unfolds into 6 squares of 4 cm², so its surface area is **24 cm²**.

A **rectangular prism** has 3 pairs of matching faces: SA = 2(lw + lh + wh).

For 3 by 2 by 1: 2(6 + 3 + 2) = **22 square units**.

A **square pyramid** net is 1 square plus 4 triangles.

With base 4 cm and triangle height 3 cm: 16 + 4 × 6 = **40 cm²**.

learn.keyIdea: Unfold the shape into its net, find the area of each face, and add them all up.

examples.title: Cube net
examples.prompt: A cube has edges of 3 cm. What is its surface area in square centimeters?

steps.do: Unfold the cube: its net is 6 squares.
steps.why: Every face of a cube is the same square.
Each face is 3 cm by 3 cm.
Surface area adds up every face.

examples.mistake: Don't find the volume (3 × 3 × 3 = 27); surface area covers the outside.

examples.title: Box surface
examples.prompt: A rectangular prism is 4 in by 3 in by 2 in. What is its surface area in square inches?

steps.why: Matching faces come in pairs.
These two faces are the same size.
The last pair of faces.
Surface area is the total of all 6 faces.

examples.mistake: Count each face pair twice; forgetting the ×2 gives only half the surface.

examples.title: Pyramid net
examples.prompt: A square pyramid has base 6 cm on a side, and each triangle face has height 5 cm. What is its surface area in square centimeters?

steps.why: The bottom of the net is a square.
Each side face is a triangle with base 6.
There is 1 square and 4 triangles in the net.

examples.mistake: Don't forget the ½ for each triangle face.

guided.prompt: A cube has edges of 5 in. What is its surface area in square inches?

steps.do: How many squares are in the net of a cube?
steps.why: A net shows every face laid flat.

steps.do: Find the area of one face: 5 × 5.
steps.why: Every face is a 5 by 5 square.
All six faces are the same size.

guided.prompt: A rectangular prism is 5 m by 2 m by 6 m. What is its surface area in square meters?

steps.why: This is the top face.
This is the front face.
This is a side face.
Each face has a matching partner.

guided.prompt: A square pyramid has base 10 ft on a side, and each triangle face has height 12 ft. What is its surface area in square feet?

steps.why: The base is a square.
Each side face is a triangle.
The net has 1 square and 4 triangles.

guided.prompt: A triangular prism has right-triangle ends with legs 3 cm and 4 cm and long side 5 cm. It is 10 cm long. What is its surface area in square centimeters?

steps.why: The prism has two matching triangle faces.
Each side of the triangle makes a rectangle 10 cm long.
Surface area is all the faces together.
